Test if filesystem backups from the fcrepo home of a live repository could be used to reliably restore the repository.
Steps:
Spin up a fedora repository.
Use multiple client scripts to load test data to the repository
Backup the fcrepo home directory while load scripts are actively ingesting new objects.
Use the backup to start a new fcrepo repository.
Verify that the repository starts without any issues (such as leveldb getting corrupted).
Make the tests repeatable

comments.body: Yes, the "Make the tests repeatable" is very important. If you could script this work, that would be helpful.

PR created: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-vagrant/pull/28

All live backups restored successfully. There were some stacktraces related to ActiveMQ which I need to investigate further.

I will update the confluence page with results soon.

Is this ready for review?
Also, since it sounds like you did not hit any issues, it would be valuable to further explore the following:

  • Real issue hit by a user who ran out of disk space and had a corrupted LevelDB
  • LevelDB backup, i.e.
    • https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/leveldb/9dftnHN7z5w
    • http://stackoverflow.com/questions/12939927/does-leveldb-supports-hot-backups-or-equivalent

Please feel free to create new tickets for these, Mohamed Mohideen Abdul Rasheed
I have made some small updates to the scripts. This is ready for review now.
Andrew Woods, can you help me get the corrupt LevelDB from the user for testing?
Reviewed on December 10 Tech Call, and we're curious if there is any updates on this.

Nick Ruest, After the initial work confirming that leveldb hot backups work, we decided that this issue is completed. We created FCREPO-1816 Closed to verify the reliability and consistency of the leveldb backups, which is currently in review with Andrew Woods.

Cool. Thanks Mohamed Mohideen Abdul Rasheed!

I'll leave it up to Andrew Woods to adjust this ticket as needed.

This looks good; however, I am unable to complete the hot_backup_runner.sh command due to "out of space" errors. Is there a way of capping the required disk usage so that the test can complete? If not, how much total disk is required?
